source_evidence: Carefully read all of the fund’s available information, including its registration statement, prospectus, and any recent 10-Ks, 10-Qs, and 8-Ks.
answer: Before evaluating a publicly traded BDC, review its available disclosures, including its registration statement, prospectus, and recent 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K filings. Also examine the fund’s fees and expenses and consider whether its investment strategy fits your goals. Useful due-diligence questions include what companies it invests in, what kinds of loans it makes, its major risks, how much debt it has taken on, and whether it has consistently paid distributions.
